title: Calculus intuition: from rates to a tangent

turns.message: I'll guess: the derivative at x=3 is the function value 9.
I’m stuck; how does shrinking h turn a secant into a tangent?
Correct answer: the derivative is the limiting slope, so x² at x=3 has slope 6, not height 9.
/verify A removable hole can have a well-defined limit even though the function is undefined at that point.

expectations.notes: Separate a function value from a rate of change and retain units where useful; use two-sided shrinking offsets to motivate the derivative and removable-hole limit; correct the height-versus-slope misconception without skipping the prediction.
